title: Bit Manipulation & Bitmask Tricks — Depth Pass
relevance: High (second ladder after XOR/popcount/`2^n` basics — the CF/AtCoder “bits are independent / rewrite with ⊕ and &” observations that dominate Div2 C–D and still appear as OA twists)
company_notes: Sum & XOR reconstruct (any array/pair with given sum and XOR) — Make Good / Vlad algebra; common phone-screen follow-up to Single Number. Pair counts with bit target (pairs XOR/sum to a power of two) — 702B / Arpa-style hash maps; Amazon OA staple. Maximize OR/AND under k moves — Orray / Boboniu / Iva & Pav (“flip ≤k bits” or OR a subset to maximize score). Online max XOR — maintain a set, answer max XOR with x — Vasiliy / trie; interview form of maximum XOR of two numbers in an array.

phases.goal: Spot depth-pass bit problems where hidden algebra, range AND/OR/XOR, progressive OR, or XOR trie/basis replaces basic Single-Number / popcount templates.

must_hit.point: After Single-Number / Fedor / Rock-and-Lever / Elevator-style templates, contest bit problems hide algebra: rewrite sum as (a⊕b)+2(a&b), force a nonzero total XOR by flipping one cell, maximize progressive OR by taking the element that sets the most new high bits, or build a binary trie / linear basis for max XOR under updates / among subsets.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names at least one of those hidden asks (sum↔XOR identity, force nonzero XOR, progressive OR, trie/basis) instead of a plain Single-Number template.

must_hit.point: Recognize them when constraints are bit-width (≤30/≤60), when AND/OR/XOR of a range or of all subarrays appears, or when you may only flip/OR/AND with a small menu of values.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites ≤30/≤60 bit-width, range/subarray AND/OR/XOR, or a small flip/OR/AND menu as the cue.

must_hit.point: OA/interview skins include sum & XOR reconstruct (Make Good / Vlad), pairs XOR/sum to a power of two (702B), maximize OR/AND under k moves (Orray / Boboniu / Iva & Pav), and online max XOR with a maintained set (Vasiliy / trie).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the prompt to one of those four skins from Where it appears.

probes: What rewritten bit algebra or constraint cue says this is depth-pass bits rather than a plain XOR/popcount/`2^n` template?
If you see ≤30/≤60 bit-width, range AND/OR/XOR, or a small flip/OR/AND menu, what do you reach for?

hints.1: Ask whether the statement hides sum↔XOR algebra, progressive OR, range AND/OR/XOR, or max-XOR under updates/subsets instead of naming a basic template.
hints.2: Cue triad: bit-width ≤30/≤60; AND/OR/XOR of a range or of all subarrays; flip/OR/AND from a small menu of values.
hints.3: Say: rewrite (a⊕b)+2(a&b); force nonzero total XOR by one flip; progressive OR / trie / linear basis; skins are sum-XOR reconstruct, power-of-two pairs, OR/AND under k moves, and online max XOR.

phases.goal: Choose the right rewrite—sum/XOR/AND identity, monotone range AND, progressive OR, range max-XOR closed form, trie, or linear basis—before coding.

must_hit.point: Sum↔XOR↔AND: a+b=(a⊕b)+2(a&b); Vlad given x=a⊕b=(a+b)/2 ⇒ a&b=x/2 (impossible if x odd or (x/2)&x≠0); Make Good appends using the same identity so new sum=2·xor.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the identity and either Vlad’s a&b=x/2 with the odd/overlap fail, or Make Good’s sum=2·xor append.

must_hit.point: Range AND is monotone under extension: binary-search / sparse-table the farthest r with AND[l..r]≥k (Iva & Pav).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States monotonicity and farthest-r search (binary search or sparse table) for AND≥k.

must_hit.point: Progressive OR: at most B≈30 useful picks; always grab the unused a_i maximizing cur|a_i, then dump the rest (Orray).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States ≤B≈30 / ≤30 meaningful OR improvements and greedy max cur|a_i.

must_hit.point: Max XOR in [L,R]: take the highest bit where L and R differ, then set all lower bits to 1 (Little Girl)—answer (1<<(msb+1))−1; no need to try every pair.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the MSB-where-L-R-differ rule and rejects pairwise enumeration.

must_hit.point: Prefix XOR + equal segment XOR (AGAGA): split into ≥2 contiguous parts with equal XOR ⇒ total XOR 0 or a three-way repeat of the same prefix value.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States total XOR 0 or the same prefix value appearing in a three-way repeat.

probes: How do you rewrite sum/XOR/AND, farthest range-AND, or progressive OR before coding?
When do you use a closed-form [L,R] max XOR, AGAGA prefix conditions, a binary trie, or a linear basis?

hints.1: Look for a sum↔XOR identity, monotone AND, OR saturation, or max-XOR structure before brute force.
hints.2: Vlad/Make Good → (a⊕b)+2(a&b); Iva & Pav → farthest r with AND≥k; Orray → ≤B≈30 greedy OR; Little Girl → MSB differ then lower bits 1; AGAGA → total XOR 0 or triple prefix.
hints.3: Say: a&b=x/2 with odd/overlap fail; binsearch/sparse farthest AND; always take max cur|a_i then dump rest; (1<<(msb+1))−1; ≥2 equal-XOR parts via total 0 or three-way prefix repeat.

phases.goal: Show the cold identities, XOR-trie / linear-basis mechanics, and constructive bit walks interviewers ask to sketch.

must_hit.point: Rewrite identities cold: a+b=(a⊕b)+2(a&b), a|b=(a⊕b)+(a&b), a&b=(a+b−(a⊕b))/2.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites at least the sum identity and one of the OR/AND companion forms.

must_hit.point: XOR binary trie (30–31 bits): child [0/1], subtree counts for delete; walk MSB→LSB preferring the opposite bit; insert/delete for online max XOR (Vasiliy).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes MSB→LSB opposite-bit walk and subtree counts enabling delete.

must_hit.point: Linear basis: bas[b]=vector with highest bit b; insert by reducing against existing basis MSB-greedy; max subset XOR by greedily OR-in; #distinct subset XORs=2^{rank} (CSES Maximum Xor Subset).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States MSB-greedy insert/reduce and greedy max query (and may cite 2^{rank}).

must_hit.point: Dima and a Bad XOR: pick first row arbitrarily; if total XOR 0, swap one cell in a row that has a differing entry to force nonzero matrix XOR.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes arbitrary first row then one differing-cell swap when total XOR is 0.

must_hit.point: Bit flips on 1..n: bit k toggles every 2^k steps → closed form for Johnny-style rating-drop counts; xor-MST bit b contributes ⌊n/2^{b+1}⌋·2^b + max(n % 2^{b+1} − 2^b, 0) (959E).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives the per-bit 2^k toggle closed form and/or the 959E per-bit contribution formula.

probes: Write the sum/XOR/AND identities and sketch an XOR-trie query or linear-basis insert.
How do you force a nonzero matrix XOR, or count 1..n bit flips / xor-MST cost without building the graph?

hints.1: Start from the three rewrite identities, then trie children or bas[b] reduction.
hints.2: Trie → 30–31 bits, prefer !bit, subtree counts for delete; basis → reduce MSB-first, greedy max; Dima → swap one differing cell if total XOR 0.
hints.3: Say: a+b=(a⊕b)+2(a&b) and companions; trie MSB→LSB opposite bit; bas[b] insert/reduce and 2^{rank}; Johnny 2^k toggles; 959E ⌊n/2^{b+1}⌋·2^b + max(n%2^{b+1}−2^b,0).

phases.goal: Match feasible tools—O(1) AND sparse table, ≤30 OR saturation steps, O(B log n) floor counts—to the constraint instead of naive loops.

must_hit.point: Range AND tools: sparse table (O(1)), or binsearch + rolling AND; never recompute naively per query.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(1) sparse table or binsearch+rolling AND and rejects naive per-query recomputation.

must_hit.point: Progressive OR / bit saturation: at most one useful improvement per bit position (≤B steps / ≤30 meaningful moves); then dump the rest.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Caps useful OR picks at ≤B / ≤30 and stops after saturation.

must_hit.point: When simulating 1..n bit flips or xor-MST on a path of integers, prefer O(B log n) floor-counting formulas over loops to n.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects looping to n and cites O(B log n) floor-counting.

probes: For many range-AND queries, what complexity is acceptable and what recomputation is forbidden?
Why is progressive OR only ≤30 useful moves, and when do you prefer O(B log n) floor counts over looping to n?

hints.1: Match the tool to query shape versus bit-width saturation versus closed-form counting.
hints.2: Many AND queries → sparse O(1) or binsearch+rolling; OR maximize → ≤B/≤30 greedy picks; 1..n flips / xor-MST → O(B log n) floors.
hints.3: Say: never recompute AND naively; ≤30 meaningful OR moves then dump rest; prefer O(B log n) floor-counting over loops to n.

phases.goal: Catch Vlad impossibility, fake full simulation, AGAGA/AND-Sequences conditions, and naive AND / pair-enumeration traps.

must_hit.point: Vlad: given x=a⊕b=(a+b)/2, setting a&b=x/2 fails if x is odd or (x/2)&x≠0 (AND overlaps XOR bits).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States both failure conditions: odd x and (x/2)&x≠0.

must_hit.point: Fortune Telling: only the parity of the array XOR vs y matters—kills fake “simulate all ops” traps.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects full simulation and cites XOR parity vs y.

must_hit.point: AND Sequences: AND of all must appear ≥2 times; then (cnt)·(cnt−1)·(n−2)! permutations—missing the ≥2 placement fails.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Requires global AND appearing ≥2 times before the factorial count.

must_hit.point: Little Girl max XOR in [L,R]: do not try every pair—MSB where L,R differ then lower bits 1 gives (1<<(msb+1))−1.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects pairwise search and states the closed form.

must_hit.point: Range AND: never recompute naively per query—use sparse table (O(1)) or binsearch + rolling AND.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names sparse/binsearch tools and forbids naive per-query AND.

probes: When is Vlad’s a&b=x/2 construction impossible?
What goes wrong if you simulate all Fortune Telling ops, skip the ≥2 global-AND placement, or enumerate all [L,R] pairs for max XOR?

hints.1: Check odd/overlap on Vlad, parity-only Fortune Telling, and ≥2 AND placement.
hints.2: Vlad → odd or (x/2)&x≠0; Fortune Telling → XOR parity vs y only; AND Sequences → AND appears ≥2 times; Little Girl → no every-pair try.
hints.3: Also: AGAGA needs total XOR 0 or a three-way prefix repeat; range AND needs sparse O(1) or binsearch+rolling, never naive recomputation.

tradeoffs.topic: Sum/XOR/AND identity rewrite vs simulating constructions
tradeoffs.strong_answer: a+b=(a⊕b)+2(a&b) (and a|b=(a⊕b)+(a&b), a&b=(a+b−(a⊕b))/2) lets Vlad recover a&b=x/2 and Make Good append so new sum=2·xor—prefer the identity over trial simulation.

tradeoffs.topic: Sparse-table O(1) range AND vs binsearch + rolling AND vs naive per-query AND
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Range AND is monotone under extension; use sparse table (O(1)) or binsearch + rolling AND for farthest r with AND≥k (Iva & Pav)—never recompute naively per query.

tradeoffs.topic: Progressive OR saturation (≤B/≤30 picks) vs sorting the whole array by OR contribution once
tradeoffs.strong_answer: At most B≈30 useful picks / ≤30 meaningful moves: always grab unused a_i maximizing cur|a_i, then dump the rest (Orray)—OR saturation, not a full static sort.

tradeoffs.topic: Closed-form max XOR in [L,R] vs trying every pair
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Highest bit where L and R differ, then set all lower bits to 1 → (1<<(msb+1))−1 (Little Girl); no need to try every pair.

tradeoffs.topic: O(B log n) floor-counting vs looping to n for bit flips / xor-MST
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Bit k toggles every 2^k on 1..n; xor-MST bit b contributes ⌊n/2^{b+1}⌋·2^b + max(n % 2^{b+1} − 2^b, 0)—prefer O(B log n) floor-counting formulas over loops to n.

tradeoffs.topic: XOR binary trie vs linear basis for max XOR
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Trie (30–31 bits, insert/delete, prefer !bit) answers online max x⊕element (Vasiliy); linear basis (MSB-greedy insert, #distinct subset XORs=2^{rank}) answers max subset XOR (CSES Maximum Xor Subset)—pick by updates vs subsets.

gotchas.trap: Using Vlad’s a&b=x/2 when x is odd or (x/2)&x≠0.
gotchas.correction: Impossible if x odd or AND overlaps XOR bits; only then set a&b=x/2 from x=a⊕b=(a+b)/2.
Only the parity of the array XOR vs y matters.

gotchas.trap: Building AND Sequences permutations without the global AND appearing ≥2 times.
gotchas.correction: AND of all must appear ≥2 times; then (cnt)·(cnt−1)·(n−2)! permutations.

gotchas.trap: Enumerating every pair for max XOR in [L,R].
gotchas.correction: Take the highest bit where L and R differ, set all lower bits to 1 → (1<<(msb+1))−1 (Little Girl).

gotchas.trap: Recomputing range AND naively per query.
gotchas.correction: Use sparse table (O(1)) or binsearch + rolling AND; AND is monotone under extension.

gotchas.trap: Checking only total XOR 0 for AGAGA equal-XOR partitions.
gotchas.correction: Split into ≥2 contiguous equal-XOR parts ⇒ total XOR 0 or a three-way repeat of the same prefix value.

gotchas.trap: Looping to n for Johnny-style bit flips or xor-MST cost.
gotchas.correction: Prefer O(B log n) floor-counting: bit k toggles every 2^k; bit b costs ⌊n/2^{b+1}⌋·2^b + max(n % 2^{b+1} − 2^b, 0).
